findings.title: NameError: response undefined when claude provider loses stream file
findings.description: In atlasforge_conductor.py invoke_llm(), when provider='claude' and _stream_file is falsy (stream registration failed), neither the if-branch (claude+stream_file) nor the elif (codex) nor the else branch is taken. The variable `response` is never assigned before line 808 uses response[:200]. This causes an unhandled NameError that crashes the LLM invocation path.
reproduction_steps: Trigger a condition where agent_stream_manager.register_agent() raises an exception (e.g., import error or socket error), causing _stream_file=None
Line 808: logger.info(f'...{response[:200]}...') raises NameError: name 'response' is not defined
findings.suggested_fix: Initialize response='' before the if/elif/else block at line 780, or add an else branch for the (claude, no stream_file) case that reads stdout

findings.title: AttributeError on None evaluator_reasoning in MissionDriftResult.from_dict
findings.description: MissionDriftResult.evaluator_reasoning is typed as str but from_dict() does not guard against non-string values. If a serialized result has evaluator_reasoning=null (None), from_dict() passes it through, and _update_tracking_state() calls result.evaluator_reasoning.startswith() which raises AttributeError on None. This bypasses the error-suppression logic, causing the drift validator to crash instead of treating it as an inconclusive result.
reproduction_steps: AttributeError raised at line 568 on result.evaluator_reasoning.startswith()
findings.suggested_fix: In from_dict(), add a guard: if not isinstance(data.get('evaluator_reasoning'), str): data['evaluator_reasoning'] = ''

findings.title: CSS selector injection via localStorage healthFilter in modals.js
findings.description: loadRecSortState() reads currentHealthFilter from localStorage and directly interpolates it into a CSS selector string at line 85: document.querySelector('.rec-health-stat.${currentHealthFilter.replace('_', '-')}') without sanitization. An attacker who can write to localStorage (XSS, browser extension, malicious page in same origin) can inject arbitrary CSS selector syntax, causing DOMException crashes or unintended element selection.
reproduction_steps: Open browser developer console on the dashboard
Run: localStorage.setItem('rec_sort_filter_state', JSON.stringify({version:2, healthFilter:'] .evil', sortField:'priority_score', sortDirection:'desc', tagFilter:''}))
loadRecSortState() interpolates the string, calling document.querySelector('.rec-health-stat.] .evil') which throws a DOMException SyntaxError
findings.suggested_fix: Validate healthFilter against a fixed allowlist of known health status values before using it in querySelector, or use CSS.escape()

findings.title: CSS selector injection in filterByHealth() via same unvalidated currentHealthFilter
findings.description: filterByHealth() at line 1132 has the identical CSS selector injection vulnerability as line 85: the status parameter (set from currentHealthFilter loaded from localStorage) is interpolated into document.querySelector without sanitization.
reproduction_steps: Same localStorage manipulation as the previous finding
Trigger filterByHealth() with a malicious currentHealthFilter value
findings.suggested_fix: Validate status against a fixed allowlist: const VALID_HEALTH = new Set(['healthy','stale','orphaned','needs_review','hot']); if (!VALID_HEALTH.has(status)) return;

findings.title: Negative integer env vars accepted by _safe_int_env without clamping
findings.description: _safe_int_env() in context_watcher.py catches ValueError but allows negative integers through. TIME_BASED_HANDOFF_MINUTES=-1, STAGE_TIMEOUT_MINUTES=-999, etc. are silently accepted. Negative handoff minutes cause immediate spurious handoffs; negative inactivity thresholds trigger constant inactivity detection; negative max absolute timeout disables the safety bound.
reproduction_steps: The time-based handoff logic fires immediately on every check since elapsed_minutes > -1 is always True
findings.suggested_fix: Add lower-bound clamping in _safe_int_env or at each call site: e.g., TIME_BASED_HANDOFF_MINUTES = max(1, _safe_int_env('TIME_BASED_HANDOFF_MINUTES', 55))

findings.title: AttributeError when mission created_at is None in archive_mission_transcripts fallback
findings.description: In af_engine/core/archival.py archive_mission_transcripts(), when mission_id is empty/None, the fallback at line 522-524 calls mission.get('created_at', datetime.now().isoformat()). If created_at is explicitly stored as None in the mission dict (not missing, but null), .get() returns None (not the default), and then None.replace() at line 523 raises AttributeError inside the outer try block, returning a failure dict with no errors listed.
reproduction_steps: Outer except catches it but result['errors'] remains [] — silent failure
findings.suggested_fix: Add: created_at = mission.get('created_at') or datetime.now().isoformat() to handle both None and missing values

findings.title: extract_insights passes None response to _extract_json, causing silent failure
findings.description: web_researcher.py extract_insights() calls invoke_fresh_llm() and passes the result directly to _extract_json() without checking for None. When invoke_fresh_llm returns (None, error_string), _extract_json(None) is called: json.loads(None) raises TypeError, which is caught and logged only at DEBUG level. The function returns {} silently with no indication to callers that the LLM call failed.
reproduction_steps: Configure WebResearcher with timeout_seconds=0 or an unreachable endpoint
Caught at line 506; returns {} with only a DEBUG log
findings.suggested_fix: Check: if response is None: return {}  before calling _extract_json

findings.title: api_add_recommendation accepts unbounded suggested_cycles with no validation
findings.description: In dashboard_modules/core.py api_add_recommendation(), suggested_cycles is taken from user JSON input with no bounds check (data.get('suggested_cycles', 3)), stored directly. The update endpoint validates 1-10, but the add endpoint does not, allowing values like -1, 0, or 999999 to be stored and later used to configure mission cycle budgets.
reproduction_steps: When mission is launched from this recommendation, cycle budget is -1
findings.suggested_fix: Add validation: cycles = max(1, min(int(data.get('suggested_cycles', 3)), 10)) with a try/except around the int() conversion

findings.title: extract_insights called with empty results list wastes an LLM call
findings.description: extract_insights() does not guard against an empty results list. When called directly with [], results_text is an empty string and a full LLM call is made asking it to analyze zero results. While the outer research_topic() guards this at line 566, direct callers of extract_insights have no protection.
reproduction_steps: LLM is invoked with a prompt containing no results; returns hallucinated/empty insights
findings.suggested_fix: Add guard at start of extract_insights: if not results: return {}
